A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaIR work, with readable and matchable methods, equations, figures, and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; both refer detailed experimental settings to supplementary materials outside the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original MaIR evaluations on super-resolution, denoising, deblurring, and dehazing, together with component ablations and stripe-width experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds aggregation-ablation results and a qualitative scanning-strategy comparison.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same architecture, NSS scanning and stripe shifts, selective scan operation, SSA aggregation, reconstruction procedures, and losses. The added aggregation alternatives are experimental comparators, not changes to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same training and evaluation datasets across all four restoration tasks. Figure 9 adds a visual case study without documenting a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Table 8 adds four SSA comparators: UVM, CAGat, FPixGat, and DWPixGat. The earlier Gating comparator is retained as SeqGat; Hilbert in Table 7 becomes Peano-Hilbert/PH. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The expanded SSA experiment introduces additional aggregation configurations and explicitly describes keeping model sizes similar for comparison. This extends the ablation design; the PDFs establish no changes to the retained benchmark splits, scales, noise levels, or metrics, nor that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.5.1 extends the existing SSA ablation with SSM-based aggregation and channel- and pixel-wise gating alternatives. New Section 4.5.2 and Figure 9 examine scanning-related texture artifacts visually. The existing NSS and stripe-width analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added ablation entries follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds PSNR/SSIM pairs for UVM (32.59/0.9324), CAGat (32.71/0.9335), FPixGat (31.90/0.9250), and DWPixGat (32.74/0.9342). Matched Gating/SeqGat SSIM changes from 0.9252 to 0.9352, with PSNR remaining 32.92. Figure 9 adds qualitative results; the other tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions and loss equations in Section 3 are unchanged. Renaming Hilbert to Peano-Hilbert and rewriting the stripe-width list do not introduce new definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning locality, continuity, long-range dependencies, computational efficiency, and performance across four tasks, 14 benchmarks, and 40 baselines.

C2.justification: Figure 9 adds concrete artifact interpretations: window-based scanning disrupts relationships between scarf regions, S-shaped scanning warps local textures, and Z-shaped scanning exhibits both problems. These extend v1's general locality-and-continuity explanation. No substantive new limitations are stated.

D1.justification: v1 promises code after acceptance; v2 states that code is available and supplies a concrete repository URL. The added ablation descriptions identify the aggregation mechanisms and convolution types. Detailed experimental settings remain deferred to supplementary materials absent from both PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and overall research positioning remain the same. DAGL's author names are corrected and its reference is reordered, causing citation renumbering. UVM-Net's additional experimental use does not introduce a new cited work or redefine the novelty claims.

P1.justification: v2 revises the author and affiliation block, identifies corresponding authors, adds acknowledgments and a short verification subsection, and edits the ablation discussion. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 9, expands Table 8 into two blocks, and corrects its caption from NSS to SSA. Figure 5 moves from page 6 to page 5, and Table 9 moves from page 9 to page 10. The remaining visual designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional aggregation comparisons strengthen support for SSA, while Figure 9 makes the scanning rationale more concrete. The code-access information and corrected Table 8 caption also improve usability. These are limited gains: the method and main benchmark evidence are unchanged, and the missing supplementary settings and underspecified visual-comparison setup still limit reproducibility.
